name: answer-from-knowledge
description: Answer questions only from the business's own facts (hours, rules, FAQ, catalog), in your own words, and never guess: log a follow-up with the exact question when something isn't there.

outline.overview:
I answer questions only from the business's own facts: hours, rules, FAQ and
catalog. When something isn't there I never guess; I say so and arrange a
follow-up with the question.

It suits any agent that speaks for a business. It is not for general advice.

It needs a facts pack for the business. It only saves something when a
follow-up is needed.

steps.title: Find it in the facts
steps.text: I look in the business's rules, FAQ and catalog.

steps.title: Answer in my own words
steps.text: Only the part that answers the question, never read word for word.

steps.title: Suggest, don't list
steps.text: Two or three options at most, then I ask what they prefer.

steps.title: Don't guess the rest
steps.text: If it isn't there, I say so and offer a follow-up with their question.

outline.needs: a business facts pack with rules, FAQ and catalog.
outline.produces: answers grounded in the business's facts, or one logged follow-up.

name: booking-with-availability
description: Take a booking or appointment during a conversation: work out the exact date, check real availability in the records, read back once, save, and send a confirmation.

outline.overview:
I take a booking or appointment: I work out the exact date, check real
availability, read it back once, save it, and send a confirmation.

It suits restaurants, salons, clinics and anyone with slots. Groups above the
business's limit get a follow-up instead of a booking.

It needs a records skill with availability and bookings, and a messaging skill
for the confirmation.

steps.title: Work out the date and time
steps.text: I turn "tomorrow" or "Saturday" into a calendar date from today's date.

steps.title: Check availability
steps.text: I check the exact slot in the records before reading anything back.

steps.title: Collect the rest
steps.text: Party size or service, and a name.

steps.title: Read it back once
steps.text: Date, time, size and name in one line.

steps.title: Save and confirm
steps.text: I save the booking, then send the confirmation with its reference.

steps.title: Handle changes
steps.text: A change after saving becomes a change request, never a second booking.

outline.needs: a records skill with availability and bookings, a messaging skill, and the business's booking rules.
outline.produces: a saved booking with its reference, and a confirmation sent.

name: caller-details-readback
description: Collect the details a booking, order or message needs without echoing each one, then read everything back once before saving, offering the caller's own number by its last four digits.

outline.overview:
I collect the details a booking, order or message needs without repeating each
one back, then read everything back once, in one quick line, before anything is
saved.

It suits any phone flow that saves something for the caller, who hears their
details once and can correct them before it counts.

It needs the caller ID. It changes nothing by itself.

steps.title: Ask for what's missing
steps.text: One question at a time, a short "okay" after each answer, and no echo.

steps.title: Offer the caller's own number
steps.text: From the caller ID, by its last four digits, inside the read-back.

steps.title: Read back once
steps.text: One line with the key details and the number question, then I wait for yes.

steps.title: Act on yes
steps.text: When the caller says yes, the next step saves it straight away.

outline.needs: the caller ID, and which numbers count as mobiles in your region.
outline.produces: details the caller has confirmed, ready to save.

name: confirm-from-tool-result
description: Only tell a person that something is booked, saved, sent or paid when the tool that did it returned success in this conversation; otherwise say it didn't work and fall back once.

outline.overview:
I only say something is booked, saved, sent or paid when the tool that did it
returned success in this conversation. If it fails, I say so plainly and fall
back once.

It suits every agent that changes things for people. Saying it's done when
nothing happened is the most damaging mistake an agent can make.

It needs nothing connected; each capability skill says what its success looks
like.

steps.title: Act before claiming
steps.text: I never say booked, saved, sent or paid before the tool has run.

steps.title: Check the result
steps.text: It only counts when the result matches that capability's success signal.

steps.title: Say what really happened
steps.text: Done if it succeeded; otherwise, that it didn't work.

steps.title: Fall back once
steps.text: On failure I take a way to follow up and log one follow-up, then stop retrying.

outline.needs: the success signal from each capability skill in use.
outline.produces: confirmations that always match what really happened.

name: docs-google-docs
description: Create and update Google Docs through NyxID, for written records such as summaries, notes and confirmations.

outline.overview:
I create a Google Doc or add to an existing one, for written records such as
call summaries, notes or confirmations.

It suits records people read rather than filter. For rows of data, use a sheet
or a database instead.

It needs a Google Workspace connection in NyxID.

steps.title: Find or create the doc
steps.text: I reuse the doc you name, or create a new one with a clear title.

steps.title: Write the content
steps.text: Plain headings and short paragraphs.

steps.title: Confirm it saved
steps.text: I read the document back and give you its link.

outline.needs: a Google Workspace connection in NyxID.
outline.produces: a Google Doc id and link with the new content.

name: files-google-drive
description: Store, copy and find files in Google Drive through NyxID, for receipts, exports and shared templates.

outline.overview:
I store, copy and find files in Google Drive, such as receipts, exports and
shared templates.

It suits keeping files where the team already looks. It is not a backup system.

It needs a Google Workspace connection in NyxID with access to the folder.

steps.title: Find the folder
steps.text: I look up the folder you name before saving anything.

steps.title: Save or copy the file
steps.text: Upload a new file, or copy a template to start from.

steps.title: Confirm and share the link
steps.text: I read the file back and give you its link.

outline.needs: a Google Workspace connection in NyxID with access to the folder.
outline.produces: a Drive file id and link.

name: human-follow-up
description: When a person needs something only staff can do, log one follow-up or escalation with a short factual summary and say plainly what happens next, without promising refunds, compensation or outcomes.

outline.overview:
When someone needs something only staff can do, I log one follow-up with a
short factual summary and say plainly what happens next.

I never promise refunds, compensation or outcomes only staff can decide, even
when the person says they don't need a call back.

It needs a place to log follow-ups, provided by a records skill.

steps.title: Decide which it is
steps.text: A follow-up when staff owe an answer; an escalation when a manager must handle a problem.

steps.title: Get the facts
steps.text: What they need, their name and a way to reach them.

steps.title: Log it once
steps.text: One record with a short summary and the details.

steps.title: Say what happens next
steps.text: Only what's true, for example "the manager decides on any refund".

outline.needs: a records skill to log follow-ups and escalations.
outline.produces: one follow-up or escalation record per request.

name: order-with-payment-link
description: Take an order from the business's catalog, save it, give the exact total the records calculate, and send a payment link; the order is confirmed once paid.

outline.overview:
I take an order from the business's catalog, save it, give the exact total the
records calculate, and send a payment link. The order is confirmed once paid.

It suits takeaway, pickup and simple product orders. I never make up prices or
promise a pickup before payment.

It needs a records skill, a payment-link skill and a messaging skill.

steps.title: Help them choose
steps.text: Only catalog items with a price that aren't sold out.

steps.title: Collect pickup and contact
steps.text: A pickup time and a mobile number for the payment link.

steps.title: Read the order back once
steps.text: The items, pickup time and name in one line.

steps.title: Save the order
steps.text: I save it and read the total from the saved record.

steps.title: Send the payment link
steps.text: I create the link for that exact total and text it.

steps.title: Confirm what happens next
steps.text: The total, and that the order is confirmed once they pay.

outline.needs: a records skill with the catalog and orders, a payment-link skill, a messaging skill, and the business's order rules.
outline.produces: a saved order with its total, and a payment link sent by SMS.

name: payment-link-stripe
description: Create a Stripe payment link or checkout session for one exact amount through NyxID, check whether it was paid, and expire it when an order is cancelled.

outline.overview:
I create a Stripe payment page for one exact amount, give you the link to send,
and later check whether it was paid or expire it if the order is cancelled.

It suits paying for one order, deposit or invoice by link. It is not for
subscriptions or saving cards.

It needs a Stripe connection in NyxID that can create prices and links; the
shared Stripe catalog entry is read-only today. Stripe charges its usual fees.

steps.title: Set the amount
steps.text: I take the exact amount and currency from the saved order, never my own arithmetic.

steps.title: Create the payment page
steps.text: A one-off price, then a payment link or checkout session for it.

steps.title: Hand over the link
steps.text: I return the URL for you or a messaging skill to send.

steps.title: Check or cancel
steps.text: I check whether it was paid, or expire it when the order is cancelled.

outline.needs: a Stripe connection in NyxID with write access to prices, payment links and checkout sessions.
outline.produces: a payment URL with its Stripe id, and later a paid, unpaid or expired status.

name: phone-call-closing
description: End phone calls cleanly: a short goodbye out loud first, hang up only afterwards, and never while the caller is talking or has asked to stay on.

outline.overview:
I end calls the way a person would: a short, warm goodbye first, and only then
I hang up. I never cut someone off.

It suits any voice agent that can end calls itself. Silence timeouts in the
phone platform still need their own settings.

It needs a hang-up tool and changes nothing else.

steps.title: Check they're done
steps.text: I only close once the caller has said goodbye or agreed we're finished.

steps.title: Say goodbye out loud
steps.text: One short line, such as "Okay, see you Saturday! Bye bye."

steps.title: Hang up after the goodbye
steps.text: I call hang-up only in the step after the goodbye has been said.

steps.title: Stay on when asked
steps.text: If they ask me not to hang up, I wait and keep listening.

outline.needs: the phone platform's hang-up tool.
outline.produces: calls that end only when the caller is done.

name: phone-conversation
description: How a voice agent talks on the phone: one language per call, short spoken replies, numbers said aloud, interruptions handled, and no written formatting.

outline.overview:
I talk with callers the way a friendly, relaxed front-desk person would: short
spoken replies, in one language, said the way people say them.

It suits any voice agent whose words are read aloud. It is not for chat or
email, where written formatting is fine.

It needs nothing connected and changes nothing.

steps.title: Pick the language
steps.text: The caller's first real reply decides the language for the whole call.

steps.title: Keep it spoken
steps.text: One idea per reply, usually under twenty words, then I let them talk.

steps.title: Say things the way people say them
steps.text: Dates, times, prices and phone numbers come out as a person says them.

steps.title: Handle interruptions
steps.text: If they talk over me, I let them finish and answer what they just said.

outline.needs: a voice that reads replies aloud, and the languages the business supports.
outline.produces: replies that sound natural on the phone.

name: phone-front-desk-sg
description: Skillset for one use case: an AI phone front desk for a small business in Singapore that answers calls, takes bookings and paid orders, texts confirmations and logs follow-ups. Built from reusable NyxID capability skills.

outline.overview:
This skillset is for one use case: an AI front desk that answers a small
business's phone in Singapore when the team can't pick up. It answers questions,
takes bookings and paid takeaway orders, texts confirmations and logs anything
staff must handle.

It suits restaurants, salons and clinics with one line and a short menu or
service list. It is not a call centre, cannot transfer calls to a person, and
does not include the business's own facts.

You need a Telnyx line, ElevenLabs for the voice, Notion for records, Twilio for
texts, Stripe for payments, and a facts pack for the business.

steps.title: Get a Singapore number
steps.text: A +65 line on Telnyx, with the documents Singapore requires.

steps.title: Create the voice agent
steps.text: The Telnyx assistant that answers every call.

steps.title: Choose the voice
steps.text: A natural ElevenLabs voice for your callers' languages.

steps.title: Set up the records
steps.text: Notion databases for bookings, orders, follow-ups and availability.

steps.title: Turn on text confirmations
steps.text: Booking confirmations and payment links by SMS.

steps.title: Turn on payment links
steps.text: Stripe links for takeaway orders, confirmed once paid.

steps.title: Run test calls
steps.text: You call the line and we check every flow end to end before going live.

outline.needs: Telnyx, ElevenLabs, Notion, Twilio and Stripe connections in NyxID, plus a business facts pack.
outline.produces: a live +65 phone front desk, with every booking, order and follow-up saved in Notion.

name: phone-number-sg-telnyx
description: Get a Singapore phone number on Telnyx for a voice agent and SMS, including Singapore's requirement documents, then verify it through NyxID.

outline.overview:
I walk you through getting a Singapore phone number on Telnyx and connect it to
your Telnyx voice agent once it's active.

It suits a +65 line answered by a Telnyx AI assistant. It is not instant:
Singapore numbers need approved requirement documents first.

It needs a Telnyx account with billing. Ordering happens in the Telnyx portal;
NyxID cannot order numbers today.

steps.title: Prepare the documents
steps.text: Telnyx asks for Singapore requirements, usually business registration and a local address.

steps.title: Order the number
steps.text: You search and order a +65 number in the Telnyx portal with those documents.

steps.title: Connect it to the agent
steps.text: Assign the number to the voice agent's call-control or TeXML application.

steps.title: Test it
steps.text: You place a test call and I check the agent answered.

outline.needs: a Telnyx account with billing, and your business registration and address documents.
outline.produces: an active +65 Telnyx number connected to your voice agent.

name: phone-number-sg-twilio
description: Get a Singapore phone number on Twilio for voice and SMS, including the regulatory documents Singapore requires, then verify it works through NyxID.

outline.overview:
I walk you through getting a Singapore phone number on Twilio and check it works
for calls and texts once it's active.

It suits a business that wants a local +65 line for a voice agent or SMS. It is
not instant: Singapore numbers need approved business documents first.

It needs a Twilio account with billing. Buying the number happens in Twilio's
console; NyxID cannot order numbers today.

steps.title: Prepare the documents
steps.text: Singapore requires a regulatory bundle, usually the business registration and a local address.

steps.title: Request the number
steps.text: You choose a mobile or local number in Twilio's console and submit the bundle.

steps.title: Point it at the agent
steps.text: Once approved, set the voice and messaging webhooks to your voice agent and SMS setup.

steps.title: Test it
steps.text: I send a test text and you place a test call to confirm both directions work.

outline.needs: a Twilio account with billing, and your business registration and address documents.
outline.produces: an active +65 number configured for voice and SMS.

name: records-google-sheets
description: Keep simple business records in a Google Sheet through NyxID: read rows, append new rows and update cells, confirming saves from the Sheets response.

outline.overview:
I keep simple records in a Google Sheet. I read rows, add new ones at the end
and update cells, and I only say something is saved when Sheets confirms it.

It suits a shared sheet the team already watches. It is not for many writers at
once or for calculations you need exact.

It needs a Google Workspace connection in NyxID with access to the sheet.

steps.title: Read the header
steps.text: I read the first row so every value lands in the right column.

steps.title: Look before writing
steps.text: I search existing rows to avoid duplicates.

steps.title: Append or update
steps.text: New records go at the end; changes go to the exact row.

steps.title: Confirm from Sheets
steps.text: Saved only when the response reports the updated range.

outline.needs: a Google Workspace connection in NyxID with access to the spreadsheet.
outline.produces: an appended or updated row, with the range Sheets reports.

name: records-notion
description: Keep business records in Notion databases through NyxID: look up, create and update rows, and confirm a save only from Notion's own response.

outline.overview:
I keep records such as bookings, orders and follow-ups in Notion databases. I
look rows up, add new ones and update them, and I only say something is saved
when Notion returns the saved page.

It suits small teams who already work in Notion. It is not for large data or
reporting.

It needs a Notion connection in NyxID shared with the databases. Each save adds
or changes one row.

steps.title: Learn the database
steps.text: I read its properties and types before writing anything.

steps.title: Look before writing
steps.text: I search for an existing row first, so I update instead of duplicating.

steps.title: Save the row
steps.text: I create or update exactly the fields that changed.

steps.title: Confirm from Notion
steps.text: I treat it as saved only when Notion returns the page and its id.

outline.needs: a Notion connection in NyxID with access to the database.
outline.produces: a created or updated Notion page, with its id and any formula values.

name: sms-send-telnyx
description: Send an SMS through a Telnyx connection in NyxID and check its delivery status. Use for confirmations, reminders and links when the number is on Telnyx.

outline.overview:
I send a text message from your Telnyx number to one phone number, then check
its delivery status.

It suits confirmations, reminders and links when your number lives on Telnyx.
It is not for bulk campaigns.

It needs a Telnyx connection in NyxID and a messaging-enabled Telnyx number.
Each message is billed by Telnyx.

steps.title: Check the number
steps.text: I make sure the recipient is a mobile number in international format.

steps.title: Write the text
steps.text: One short message with only what the person needs.

steps.title: Send it
steps.text: I send it from your messaging-enabled Telnyx number.

steps.title: Check delivery
steps.text: I read the message status and report sent, delivered or failed.

outline.needs: a Telnyx connection in NyxID and a messaging-enabled Telnyx number.
outline.produces: one SMS, with its Telnyx message id and delivery status.

name: sms-send-twilio
description: Send an SMS through a Twilio connection in NyxID and check whether it was delivered. Use for confirmations, reminders and payment or booking links.

outline.overview:
I send a text message from your Twilio number to one phone number, then check
whether Twilio accepted and delivered it.

It suits confirmations, reminders and links sent after a call or an order. It
is not for marketing blasts or two-way chat threads.

It needs a Twilio connection in NyxID and a Twilio number or messaging service.
Each message is billed by Twilio.

steps.title: Check the number
steps.text: I make sure the recipient is a mobile number in international format.

steps.title: Write the text
steps.text: One short message with only what the person needs, under 160 characters when possible.

steps.title: Send it
steps.text: I send it from your Twilio number or messaging service.

steps.title: Check delivery
steps.text: I read the message status and report sent, delivered or failed.

outline.needs: a Twilio connection in NyxID, the Account SID, and a sending number or messaging service.
outline.produces: one SMS, with its Twilio message SID and delivery status.

name: voice-agent-elevenlabs
description: Choose voices and create ElevenLabs conversational agents through NyxID, for heavily customised voices and web or phone voice agents.

outline.overview:
I help you pick an ElevenLabs voice and create an ElevenLabs conversational
agent with its prompt, first message and voice. I play voice samples, and you
try the agent from its page in the ElevenLabs dashboard.

It suits heavily customised voices and agents. Changing an existing agent is not
available through NyxID yet; that happens in the ElevenLabs dashboard.

It needs an ElevenLabs connection in NyxID. Usage is billed by ElevenLabs.

steps.title: Pick a voice
steps.text: I list voices that suit your languages and play a short sample.

steps.title: Create the agent
steps.text: Its prompt, first message, language and chosen voice.

steps.title: Try it
steps.text: You talk to the agent with the test button on its ElevenLabs dashboard page, then tell me what to change.

steps.title: Hand it to the phone line
steps.text: I give the voice and agent ids to the phone provider setup.

outline.needs: an ElevenLabs connection in NyxID.
outline.produces: a chosen voice id and an ElevenLabs agent id, tried in the dashboard.

name: voice-agent-telnyx
description: Create and maintain a Telnyx AI voice assistant through NyxID: instructions, greeting, model and voice, answering calls on a Telnyx number.

outline.overview:
I set up a Telnyx AI assistant that answers your phone line: its instructions,
greeting, model and voice. I can also update its instructions later.

It suits a phone agent that must answer real calls on a Telnyx number. Tools the
agent calls during a call, such as bookings and orders, are wired in the Telnyx
portal.

It needs a Telnyx connection in NyxID. Calls are billed by Telnyx.

steps.title: Find or create the assistant
steps.text: I look for an existing assistant before creating one.

steps.title: Write its instructions
steps.text: The behaviour and facts the agent follows on every call, plus its greeting.

steps.title: Choose model and voice
steps.text: A fast model and a voice that speaks your callers' languages.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: I read the assistant back and confirm the instructions and voice took effect.

outline.needs: a Telnyx connection in NyxID; a Telnyx number for real calls.
outline.produces: a Telnyx assistant id with the agreed instructions, greeting and voice.
